headline: Norway's government said it will propose a temporary ban on camera-equipped AI glasses in selected public places because of privacy concerns.
score_reason: Lowered by 1 from 5: the announcement was on about 7 Oct 2026, three days before this edition, and it is only a proposal.
importance_line: People in Norway could soon be barred from wearing camera glasses in parks, schools or gyms, and other countries may watch, but the plan still needs parliament's approval and its final scope is unclear.
summary: Road to VR reported on 7 October 2026 that Norway's Ministry of Digitization and Public Administration plans to ask parliament for a temporary ban on smart glasses in places such as parks, beaches, museums, shopping malls and spaces used by children, while still allowing them in some places and for private use. Minister Torgeir Micaelsen says the pause would give time for an informed debate and lasting rules, but the plan needs parliament's approval, so its final scope is uncertain.
notes: AP original blocked; read Road to VR and Yahoo (which cites ABC News). Announcement dated 7 Oct 2026; AP piece is 10 Oct. Not carried in earlier editions we checked.
